title.narrative: Peer 2 Peer 4 Justice, Sustaining the Indonesia- Netherlands Legal Network

description.narrative: With the phasing out of Dutch development aid in 2020, the bilateral relationship will enter a transition phase. This phase is meant to ensure that important partnerships are not abruptly cut off and that crucial relationships and networks continue to exist. This phase also allows key stakeholders to jointly map out the priorities that will shape the new bilateral relationship and the importance of a well-functioning rule of law. To this end, the Peer 2 Peer or P2P project was established. This project aims to contribute to the sustained, long term peer to peer partnerships and knowledge exchange between Indonesian and Dutch legal professionals in support of concrete justice reform areas in Indonesia. The project will run from 2019 to 2023.

title.narrative: New bilateral relations between justice sector institutions were established in support of concrete reform goals.

description.narrative: New bilateral relationships were supported through the organization of activities. Topics such as probation and alternative sanctions, access to remedy for loss of housing and impunity were part of this outcome.

title.narrative: Many activities were organized under this outcome. The focus was on 2-3 separate activities each project year. The support of the new bilateral relationship of the probation services was ongoing.

Since 2019, new bilateral relationships with judicial institutions and other (non) -government organisations have been organized. These new bilateral relationships include but are not limited to:1. Dutch probation service- Ditjen Pas2. Indonesian and Dutch universities (such as the van Vollenhove Institute and the Atma Jaya University)3. Lawyer offices such as Pels Rijcken4. Several CSO's and NGO's
Sustained and institutionalised relations of NL/IND justice sector institutions have furthered concrete reform processes.

description.narrative: Several bilateral judicial relationships were supported, such as that of the Indonesian and Dutch Supreme Court, the Indonesian and Dutch Ombudsman, the Council of the Judiciary and the Indonesian and Dutch Probation Service. Each institutions had it's own focus and held many activities.

title.narrative: Each project year, various high-level working visits were organized. These activities were both online (mainly due to COVID-19) and in-person. Next to the high-level working visits, operational activities such as analysis, training and other activities were organized.

Through this project, various key institutions in the justice sector and the justice chain have been supported. This was done through online work, in-person and high-level working missions, training, analysis, and many other activities.
The Indonesia-Netherlands Rule of Law network continues to operate and remains relevant.

description.narrative: The project has organized and been the secretary of the Indonesia-Netherlands working group. Every year several working groups were organized in person and online in the Netherlands and in Indonesia.Next to the working groups, two Indonesia-Netherlands Legal Update or INLU was organized by the project.
